content:
maria: rolled continuous-batcher-v3 to canary at 04:10 UTC, immediately saw p95 spike on short-seq workloads. reverting patch for now. :grimacing:
cheng: which metric jumped? p50/p95/throughput? any kernel fallback logs?
maria: quick numbers from canary cluster (service=serve-x, model=r-infer-small): p50 42ms -> 49ms, p95 210ms -> 530ms, tokens/s -22%. error budget still ok but SLA risk. We see a lot more singletons in batch formation.
devon: logs show kernel_selector choosing fast_attn_v2 less often; fallback to compat_attn_v1 increased. suspect the new batch formation gating changed shape signals we feed to selector.
maria: exact snippet from deploy logs: `kernel_selector: preferred=fast_attn_v2; chosen=compat_attn_v1; reason=shape_mismatch && prefill_detected`
lucas: KV cache metrics look odd too — prefill priming dropped. kv_hit_rate: 86% -> 73% in canary. Could be batching leading to more interleaved prefill vs streaming requests.
qa-bot: automated regression test (small-seq throughput) failed 3/3 runs in canary. diff shows microbatches collapsed to singles.
cheng: can we get a profiler dump around batch formation for affected pods? want: batch_size_hist, queue_wait_ms, kernel_choice_counts, kv_prefill_timing.
maria: pasted profiler excerpt from pod s-23 (1 min window right after rollout):
```
batch_size_hist = {1: 62%, 2: 28%, 3-4: 7.5%, >=5: 2.5%}
queue_wait_ms_p50 = 1.2, p95 = 4.9
kernel_choice_counts = {fast_attn_v2: 120, compat_attn_v1: 420}
kv_prefill_latency_ms = p50 6.2 -> 10.8 (during spike)
```
cheng: that's telling — the heuristic tweak bumped the token_budget_target downward for cohorts with short expected seq, causing earlier flushes and breaking the shape that fast_attn_v2 expects. fast_attn_v2 prefers batches >=3 and contiguous prefix cached.
devon: reproduced locally by forcing token_budget_target 30% lower: batch sizes collapse, kernel_selector routes to compat_attn_v1 which has higher overhead for many small singletons -> p95 explosion.
lucas: so it's the interplay: batching heuristic -> batch shapes -> kernel selection -> kv priming -> latency. multi-hop regression chain.
maria: proposed immediate mitigation: revert canary to previous heuristic (done), set a kill-switch in runtime to avoid token_budget_target changes that reduce avg_batch_size below 2.5 for short-cohorts. open to better fixes.
cheng: +1. Also add fast_attn_v2 gating: require cached_prefix_hit_rate >= 70% OR avg_batch_size >=3 to pick it. that buys us safety while tuning.
devon: I'll draft a small test harness to simulate mixed prefill/streaming traffic and validate heuristics before rollout. QA - can you add a targeted regression test for this shape?
lucas: I'll dig into why kv_prefill_latency spiked — might be prefetch scheduling collision under the new merge window.
qa-bot: created issue INF-4921: "canary: continuous-batcher-v3 causes batch collapse -> kernel fallback -> p95 spike" and attached logs.
maria: thanks team. reassigning follow-ups: devon (simulation harness), lucas (kv prefill investigation), cheng (kernel selector gating change), maria (rollout postmortem). I'll post a short summary to #eng-runtime once we have RCA. :thumbsup:
cheng: one more ask — add perf counters to detect sudden kernel_choice_shifts (delta >30% within 5m) and auto-alert so we catch this earlier next time.
maria: noted. adding alert and a dashboard row now.
